name: SAP HANA
tagline: SAP's in-memory columnar HTAP database, the mandatory engine under S/4HANA.
description: SAP HANA is an in-memory, column-oriented database that runs transactions and analytics on the same tables, and it is the only database supported by S/4HANA, which is why most of its installed base is SAP customers. Beyond SQL it bundles graph, spatial, JSON document store, a vector engine and a knowledge-graph engine, and HANA Cloud adds a data lake tier and native storage extension for warm data. On-premises customers run HANA 2.0 SPS08; HANA Cloud ships quarterly releases. Outside SAP landscapes it is rarely chosen, because RAM-sized licensing and hardware make it costly and the ecosystem is SAP-centric.

pricing.notes: On-prem licensed largely by memory; HANA Cloud billed in capacity units. HANA Cloud free tier and HANA express edition for development.

managedServices.name: SAP HANA Cloud
managedServices.provider: SAP (on AWS, Azure, GCP, Alibaba Cloud)

scale.notes: Scale-out across multiple hosts and system replication for HA/DR; capacity is bounded by expensive RAM.

strengths: Columnar in-memory storage runs analytical queries directly on live transactional data
Required and fully optimised for S/4HANA and SAP BW/4HANA
Multi-model in one engine: graph, spatial, JSON documents, vectors and knowledge graphs
Dictionary compression keeps column data several times smaller than row stores
System replication gives near-zero-RPO failover for SAP landscapes
weaknesses: Memory-based licensing and certified hardware make it expensive
Ecosystem and skills are concentrated in SAP projects
Large instances have long restart/load times despite persistence
Rarely a sensible choice for non-SAP greenfield applications
useCases: Real-time operational reporting on ERP data
Embedding analytics and ML (PAL/APL) in SAP business processes
Grounding SAP Joule/AI scenarios with the vector and knowledge-graph engines
notIdealFor: Datasets far larger than affordable RAM
Teams wanting open-source tooling and portability
